notes:
SwapCounterHook counts completed swaps, per pool, and does nothing else.

What is in the repository: src/SwapCounterHook.sol (the hook), src/HookFlags.sol (aliases of the v4-core permission-bit constants, used to mine and to check an address), src/Placeholder.sol (left from the project setup and not part of the launch), and the Foundry project the three were built in -- solc 0.8.26, evm_version cancun, optimizer on at 800 runs, bytecode_hash none, with forge-std, v4-core, v4-periphery, solmate, OpenZeppelin and permit2 vendored under lib/ as ordinary committed files. The hook's tests are test/SwapCounterHook.t.sol and test/SwapCounterHookInvariant.t.sol, which stand it up at a mined CREATE2 address against a real PoolManager and drive it through the manager rather than calling it by hand. It extends v4-periphery's BaseHook (lib/v4-periphery/src/utils/BaseHook.sol).

Permissions: afterSwap, and only afterSwap. getHookPermissions returns that one field true and the other thirteen false, so the address the hook is mined for carries exactly 0x40 (Hooks.AFTER_SWAP_FLAG, 1 << 6) and PoolManager calls exactly one callback. beforeSwap is off; both swap returnDelta flags are off, as are both liquidity ones. BaseHook's constructor validates its own address against getHookPermissions, so a deployment at an address that disagrees reverts rather than producing a hook the manager would call for a callback it does not implement.

State and reads: mapping(PoolId poolId => uint256 swaps) public swapCount, incremented by one in _afterSwap under the key derived from the PoolKey the callback was handed. The generated getter and getSwapCount(PoolId) return the same value, and both return zero for a pool the hook has never served. The count is keyed by pool id rather than global because one hook instance serves every pool that installs it.

_afterSwap returns (IHooks.afterSwap.selector, int128(0)). The int128 is zero on every path -- there is no path that computes one -- so a swap settles exactly as it would with no hook attached; with afterSwapReturnDelta off, a non-zero value there would make the manager revert. It is written as an override of BaseHook's internal _afterSwap, so the inherited onlyPoolManager check on the external afterSwap stands and a call from any other address reverts without touching the counter. swapCount[id] is therefore monotonically non-decreasing, rises by exactly one per completed swap on that pool, and is never reset, decremented, or written from anywhere else.

What the contract deliberately does not have: no owner, admin, role, or privileged address of any kind; no currency handling -- it never takes, settles, mints, transfers or holds a token or ETH, and has no receive or fallback; no withdrawal path, because there is nothing to withdraw; no fee; no pause, no proxy, no delegatecall, no selfdestruct, and no setter. Nothing about its behaviour can change after deployment, so the code that was reviewed is the code that runs.

Constructor: constructor(IPoolManager) and nothing more. The single argument above is the canonical Uniswap v4 PoolManager on Ethereum Sepolia, which this launch targets; it is baked into the creation code the hook's address is mined from, so the hook and the pool it is installed on must name the same manager or every callback would be refused.

Token: none is named, because this repository does not contain one. Its whole deliverable is the hook -- the only ERC-20 in the tree is test/mocks/MockERC20.sol, a test-only mock with an unpermissioned mint and burn, and naming that as a launch token would be false. The launched token is whatever the launch policy's factory deploys.

Pool: the launched token paired with USDC on Sepolia (0x1c7d4b196cb0c7b01d743fbc6116a902379c7238) at the 1% fee tier, whose canonical spacing is 200 ticks. Nothing in this repository pins a pool -- its tests stand pools up over freshly deployed mock currencies, across several fee tiers, purely to make the counter's key observable -- so these are the launch policy's allowlisted paired currency and fee tier, not a value read out of the code, and they are the part of this manifest a reviewer should check against the policy rather than against src/. No initial price is stated: the manifest has no field for one, and the launched token's address, and so which side of the pair it sorts to, is not known until its salt is fixed at deploy time.
